subject: Post-incident data governance questions — regional hold & minimal-slice approach
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on post-incident log hold and minimal data slices

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick response during Friday's incident. As we wrap up our internal post-mortem, our security team has a couple of follow-ups on evidence retention and transfer:

1) Jurisdictional hold — Acme needs clarity on how Redwood will store the preserved artifacts if we request a legal hold. Specifically: where (region) will the preserved data sit, and do you support object-lock / WORM controls?

2) Minimal-slice option — we prefer that only the smallest useful subset of logs / KV prefixes be preserved (to limit patient data exposure). Can Redwood produce a cryptographically-signed minimal slice, with checksums and a short manifest describing redaction steps?

3) Chain-of-custody transfer — if we ask for handoff, does Redwood provide a sealed archive with transfer receipts (signed checksums + transfer timestamp) and an option for a notarized or DocuSign-backed confirmation?

4) Retention default vs. exception — what are the standard retention windows for preserved incident artifacts (US / EU), and what is the process/lead time to request an extension?

I've attached a small sample of session IDs and an example snippet from our forensics team for context. Can you confirm what you need from us to initiate a hold vs. a normal retention extension?

Appreciate it — a quick call would work too.

Best,
Lisa Chen
Security Lead, Acme Health

Attachments: session-ids-sample.csv (csv), example-ctx.txt (text)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on post-incident log hold and minimal data slices

Lisa — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping Karthik (security/compliance) and Vanessa (Customer Success) so we can align on technical and operational next steps. Answers below at a high level; Karthik will add specifics and feasible timelines.

1) Jurisdictional hold: Redwood supports regional preservation. For hosted artifacts we can preserve copies in the region you request (US-east, EU-west) when feasible. For formal holds we use S3-compatible buckets with Object Lock enabled (WORM) and multi-region replication only if you explicitly request cross-border copies.

2) Minimal-slice: yes — we can produce a redacted/minimal slice. Our process is: identification of relevant session IDs -> KV prefix slicing -> automated redaction of detected PII -> generation of a manifest that lists slices, redaction actions, and SHA256 checksums for each file. These manifests are signed by our incident ops account. Note that certain runtime artifacts (active KV caches) require a snapshot and may include non-identifying metadata; we'll flag those in the manifest.

3) Chain-of-custody transfer: we support sealed-archive export (tar.gz) with SHA256 checksums and a signed transfer receipt. We can also coordinate a DocuSign acknowledgement for evidence handoff if you need a legal attestation. For elevated legal requests we follow our documented chain-of-custody process and can escrow copies to a third-party custodian on request.

4) Retention windows: default preserved-incident artifacts are kept 90 days in the hosted environment. For regulated customers we offer 12 months (EU) or 24 months (US) as a contractable extension; extensions require an approval ticket and may incur storage charges. Requests for longer holds (3+ years) are handled as exceptions via our Legal + Contracts team.

What we need from Acme to start a regional hold:
- Named request with scope (session IDs, org IDs, time range)
- Preferred retention region (e.g., eu-west or us-east)
- Whether you want cross-region replication
- Whether you require DocuSign/notarized transfer receipts

If that matches what you expected I can start the hold and propose an ETA (typically 24–48 hours for a minimal-slice preservation, 3–5 business days for a notarized sealed transfer).

Jordan Blake

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on post-incident log hold and minimal data slices

Hi all — adding the technical playbook and constraints so Acme has the full picture. TL;DR: we can do what you asked; a few caveats and options below.

- Snapshot mechanics: for a minimal slice we perform a time-bounded snapshot of token-level logs, request headers, and kv-cache references. We do not include model weights or full KV dumps unless explicitly requested. Snapshots are generated as compressed artifacts with per-file checksums.

- Redaction & manifest: redaction is automated via our PII detection pipeline + manual verification for high-sensitivity slices. Manifest fields: filename, sha256, redaction-summary (fields removed/hashed), producer-id, timestamp, region. All manifests are signed by our incident-ops GPG key.

- WORM & object-lock: we can place preserved artifacts into an Object Lock-enabled bucket with a legal hold tag. Once legal hold is applied, deletion is blocked until hold removal. Cross-region replication will copy objects but will not break the hold semantics in the destination region.

- Cryptographic attestation & notarization: we create a signed transfer receipt (SHA256 list + timestamp) and can wrap that with DocuSign if Acme requires a signature trail. If Acme prefers escrow with a third-party custodian (e.g., Ironclad-like custodian), we can prepare the archive and deliver via encrypted SFTP with transfer receipts.

- Timelines & costs: minimal-slice preservation: 24–48 hours. Full sealed archive + notarization: 3–5 business days. Storage and retrieval for preserved artifacts follow our standard storage pricing; legal hold extensions beyond 12 months will have an admin approval and storage surcharge.

- EU-specific note: for EU-region holds we will by default keep artifacts in eu-west and avoid cross-border replication unless you request it. For HIPAA-bound data we will apply additional access controls and audit logging.

Next steps: if Acme confirms scope + region I will request an ops job and send you an ETA and signed manifest template.

-Karthik
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
